page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96 is a general-purpose server powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 360 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 3.75 GB of memory per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. This configuration does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core performance. It achieves top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 538.12 GB/sec and static web serving throughput at 126.92 GB/sec. Geekbench multi-core, image processing, and text processing scores also rank in the top 10% tier. The processor's support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) contributes to strong performance in extended instruction tests, database operations, and LLM prompt processing. Single-core performance and memory write speeds fall into the average to strong categories.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-96 offers high compute density and advanced instruction sets without the added cost of bundled GPUs or local NVMe storage, making it resource-efficient for CPU-bound workloads. It is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, high-throughput web serving, database operations, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
